status_summary: On 2025-10-16 EPA's Office of Land and Emergency Management issued a residential soil lead directive for Superfund and RCRA cleanup sites, setting a screening level of 200 parts per million and a removal management level of 600 parts per million and superseding January 2024 guidance; it sets levels but no multi-year plan or milestones. On 2026-06-03 EPA announced a long-term Superfund Solutions initiative to speed investigations at more than 500 sites, evaluate Superfund, RCRA and Brownfields options in parallel, and begin short-term protective projects while full cleanup plans are finalized, with steps to follow over the coming months. No revision of the National Contingency Plan, no ARAR streamlining and no 10-year lead plan with milestones was found.

timeline.event: The Office of Land and Emergency Management issued a residential soil lead directive for CERCLA sites and RCRA corrective action facilities, with a 200 ppm screening level and a 600 ppm removal management level, superseding the January 2024 guidance.

EPA announced the Superfund Solutions initiative on project management, earlier use of tools and authorities including short-term protective work, and a single target blood lead level for residential lead cleanups.

title: Streamline Superfund: revise the NCP, expand removals, streamline ARARs, 10-year lead plan
uncertainties: The 2025-10-16 directive and 2026-06-03 release were read on epa.gov; the release does not mention ARARs or the National Contingency Plan and sets no deadlines or numerical targets. A 2026-06-03 proposed rule amending Superfund claims hearing procedures (removing an evidence exclusion in 40 CFR 305.31) was checked in review; it is procedural and not one of the listed items, and it does not propose rescinding the small claims arbitration rule as a law-firm summary had suggested, so it is not in the timeline. The 2025 lead levels are a different action from the 10-year plan the Mandate asks for. Whether EPA's removal program usage rose was not measured. Searches run: Federal Register API (CERCLA, contingency plan, Superfund proposed rules), and web searches on Superfund lead, NCP revision and the Superfund Solutions initiative. A direct Federal Register query with the full NCP title was rejected for length, so an NCP rulemaking could be missed; unified agenda entries were not read. A Federal Register API search for the term National Contingency Plan from 2025-01-20 (10 results, read in this pass) showed only a 2025-11-17 final rule extending the transition period for new product schedule listing, which is not a revision to streamline cleanup; no ARAR or lead plan document appeared. The directive page read does not describe its process improvements; the full directive was not opened.
